batches.note: The greenfield pieces meet at full-width 3-high cross-berms (world z=-1,-15,-16,-30) pierced only by the 3-wide path notch, so the corridor reads as three walled rooms with doorways. Drop each cross-berm to the meadow datum (62). The y-floor of each region is the walk plane, so the path spine (top solid 62) has no cell in range and is untouched by construction.

The west berm (world x=2..3) rises 3 blocks ABOVE the meadow, so the corridor's west side reads as a grass wall at eye level. Invert it into an outward fall: the rim drops below the waterline and the bank behind it to meadow height, then two smoothing passes roll the terrace into a bank. These columns never contain the path spine (world x=9..11), so the region may reach down to y=61.
The east berm (world x=17..18) mirrored: rim below the waterline, bank to meadow height, two smoothing passes. Same reasoning as the west bank — these columns never contain the path spine.

A bare graded bank still reads as earthworks. Speckle seeded stone/andesite/tuff outcrops down both banks so the fall to the water reads as eroded rock, never a uniform slope. The path spine is declared as a keep-clear envelope even though the bank regions exclude it, so the intent survives any later region edit.

Give the meadow an edge the eye reads as a boundary instead of the berm it replaced: sparse oak clusters on the OUTBOARD band where the meadow breaks into the bank, both flanks of both greenfield pieces. Count and spacing are deliberately low — a first pass at count 10 / spacing 4 closed the canopy into a leaf tunnel over the path, trading the grass wall for a green ceiling. The path spine is the keep-clear envelope, so the lean-or-grow canopy rule keeps the corridor open overhead.

The massif met the sea as a sheer 23-block face cut off square at the waterline, and a first attempt to break the face with thin cantilevered ledges failed: a shelf with air under it reads as a fin stuck to the cliff, not as weathering. Replace both with one stepped skirt — four concentric rings around the west, north and east faces and under the two south flanking walls, cresting at world y=71, 66, 63 and 61, so the cliff steps back on its way down instead of dropping in one plane. Each ring is solid rock to within two blocks of its crest and only the crest carries air weight, so the step tops are irregular while every cell still rests on rock — no floaters by construction. Gravel is deliberately absent: DW0313 refused it, since a cell at the island's base sits in the ambient water column with no substrate and a falling block would sink to the seabed. Entirely additive and entirely outside the piece, so the cavern, the mouth, the boulder gate and every anchor are untouched. The south rings stop short of the corridor mouth so the greenfield entrance is never buried.

The apron fixed the waterline but the skyline was still a flat slab with square corners. Break it upward rather than downward: the plateau is a thin crust over interior voids in places (rim columns with air one block under the top), so lowering it would punch holes into the mountain. Instead grow an undulating crest above the existing top from a rock recipe with real air weight at a coarse noise scale, so broad swells alternate with broad bare stretches. The band is only two blocks deep: a first pass five deep left detached slabs hanging over the crest, because the value noise decorrelates across that much vertical distance. Kept shallow, a crag cell and the cell under it sample nearly the same noise, so the crest stays attached to the rock. The two daylight shafts are subtracted with a one-block pad so the cavern's light wells are never capped. The region stops at the rim. Running it one block proud to ragged the plan-view outline was tried and reverted: an overhanging crest cell has nothing beneath it, so it read as a thin fin hanging in the air rather than an undercut. The plateau's outline in plan therefore stays straight — raggedding it needs material REMOVED at the rim, which is unsafe over the hollow crust and has no thickness-aware region selector to make it safe.

Where the de-walled banks and the mountain's south shelf meet the sea the land still ended on a clean grass edge. Lay sand and gravel tongues with occasional rock across the 61-64 band on both greenfield flanks and along the mountain's south shore, so the walk plane grades into the water instead of stopping at it. Scatter drops onto standable cells only, so every grain rests on real ground — the support check covers the falling blocks. The path spine is the keep-clear envelope. Round 13 owner playtest: this scatter was also dropping sand, gravel and stone ON the bottom tread row of the mountain's switchback face (piece-local z=39, eleven blocks standing on cobblestone stairs) — a staircase you climb is not a place to put dressing. The whole stepped face is now a keep-clear envelope; the other three shore rows still grade into the water.

Owner playtest finding: the beach-greenfield junction still read as a wall layer. Round 8 cut the four 65-high cross-berms (world z=-1,-15,-16,-30) but the greenfield prefab edges its pieces in TWO rows, not one: behind the 65 berm sits a 64 lip at prefab-local z=13, which no cut reached. At the strand that lip stands two blocks above both the sand and the meadow and spans ten of the thirteen non-spine columns — a wall with a doorway, exactly as reported. Worse, round 8's bank smoothing then pulled the already-cut z=14 row partly back up toward its un-cut neighbour, restoring a 63-64 step at world z=-1. Drop the lip row on both greenfield pieces and re-flatten the south edge row, then finger sand and gravel from the strand into the meadow so the material changes gradually instead of at a line. No smoothing pass here: the junction is flat at the meadow datum once the lip is gone, and smoothing is what re-raised it last time. The path spine is untouched structurally as before (every morph region's y-floor is the walk plane, so the spine columns hold no cell in range) and is declared keep-clear for the scatter on both sides of the seam. The same prefab row is levelled at the inner piece seam (world z=-17) in the same batch: it is literally the same lip, and cutting only the one the owner stood in front of would leave its twin mid-corridor.

Round-12 finding, round-13 restore: the sheep fold reads 5x5 with a 3x3 interior, but its WEST interior column (piece-local x=3) was solid in the assembled world, so the pen held six bodies instead of nine. Four west-region batches take piece-local x 0..3 as 'the west bank' while the fold rectangle is x 2..6. The three seeded batches (bank-outcrops, meadow-treeline, shore-transition) now declare the fold rectangle as a keep-clear envelope, which stops rock, sand and oaks landing inside the walls. The fourth, west-bank-falls, reshapes terrain with a morph, which carries no keep-clear, so this batch re-cuts what the smoothing pass filled: grass at the fold's west floor row and air in the three interior cells above it. Scoped to exactly nine columns per piece - it never touches the bank silhouette the morph exists to make.

Round-21 finding A (owner playtest): a sheep left the beach fold by walking OVER its wall. The fold's ring is minecraft:cobblestone_wall down the east and west sides and at the north corners, but minecraft:mossy_cobblestone - a FULL CUBE, one block high - along the middle of the north and south edges. A wall block is a 1.5-tall barrier the router may neither pass through nor stand on; a full cube is an ordinary one-block ledge every body in the dims table can hop. So the ring the player's eye reads as one enclosure is, to the route planner, impassable at nine cells and a step at five, and the flock's shortest way out of the pen ran up the east face at [7,63,-9], across the north wall's top at [7,64,-10] and down into the meadow - the pen's real opening at [6,63,-6] never used. Make the ring ONE material so the model's barrier and the player's eye agree. Five cells per greenfield piece, both pieces (the prefab is drawn twice, like batch/fold-clear): the north edge's three middles and the south edge's two, at the walk level (piece-local y=3). The openings are untouched - the south doorway at piece-local (4,3,9) and the south-west corner gap at (2,3,9) stay air, so the fold still has a way in and out, and it is now the only way.

Round-21 finding B (owner playtest): the flock walks through the mountain pen's fence gate and the player cannot. [18,73,-63] shipped minecraft:oak_fence_gate[facing=east,open=false]. Two defects in one cell. (1) ORIENTATION: the pen's south fence line runs east-west, so the gate belongs on the Z axis (facing north/south, vanilla's Z_SHAPE: full across X, thin in Z). facing=east gives it X_SHAPE instead - a leaf standing edge-on in the doorway, spanning the cell's full depth at x 18.375..18.625 - which is why walking straight through it was impossible and offsetting to x~18.0 squeezed past. (2) STATE: closed. A closed gate is passable for the PLAYER, who right-clicks it open, and for nobody else; a move-npc/move-actor puppet is a tp polyline that performs no interaction, and no runtime verb changes a fence gate's block state, so a gate shipped closed is closed for the whole delve. Sixteen walked legs crossed it anyway. Ship it open and square to the line: an open fence gate has no collision at all, so the same route becomes honest for puppet and player alike. DW0452 is the proof that now holds this.

Owner ruling 2026-08-06: the meadow banks are MEANT to get their feet wet. The two bank-falls batches roll the berms down past the waterline, so the outermost bank columns of both greenfield pieces stand at world y=62 - the ocean line - and the delivered world takes them. Declare that: the west and east bank bands of both pieces (piece-local x 0..3 and 13..16, y 0..2) are the envelope the ambient sea is admitted into, and the compiler computes which cells it actually reaches (25) and materializes them as water instead of leaving the shoreline to first-boot fluid ticks. The envelope is an ENVELOPE, not a claim of wetness: it also contains one cell the sea cannot reach - a sealed one-block pocket in piece 2's west bank at piece-local [1,2,10] that two smoothing passes left dry a block under the waterline - and DW0364 goes on refusing that cell until this batch fills it back to the bank surface. The fill runs first so the flood sees the finished bank.
